openQuestions.q: B-d8ef and B-4a78 are cited by story ID in understanding.json but no docs/requirements/decisions/ file matches those story IDs by title. Is there a specific decisions/ doc backing them, or is this a completed-story cross-reference with no standing spec doc?
openQuestions.evidence: understanding.json facts cite B-d8ef (canonicalReviewHostLauncherSpec freeze) and B-4a78 (signed readManifest coordination); grep for both story IDs across docs/requirements/decisions/*.md returned zero matches. The concrete touchpoints they describe (canonicalReviewHostLauncherSpec, launcherArgvMatchesCanonical) were verified present today in packages/main/src/core/host-execution-readiness.ts, so the underlying work appears real and already landed; it just is not backed by a discoverable decisions/ doc under those names.
openQuestions.resolution: B-d8ef and B-4a78 are deliberately cited as story-ID provenance, not as decisions/ specs: their mechanical contracts live in merged source (canonicalReviewHostLauncherSpec / launcherArgvMatchesCanonical in packages/main/src/core/host-execution-readiness.ts, and the readManifest normalization in packages/main/src/core/reviewer-read-evidence.ts), which the scope reviewer verified present. The governing decisions/ spec for this story is lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md; no additional decisions/ doc is required for story-to-story build-on references.

openQuestions.q: CHK-004 assumes reviewer_batch guidance currently prints raw codex exec/claude --print/agy --print launch instructions that need rewriting to name lattice host_run. Does this guidance text exist today, and if so where?
openQuestions.evidence: grep for 'codex exec', 'claude --print', 'agy --print' in packages/main/src/handlers/reviewer-batch.ts returned no matches. The rewrite scope described in CHK-004 could not be located in that file; it may live in a different file, be templated, or be smaller than described. Not treated as a scope gap because CHK-004's own verification step (rg check for remaining raw-launch strings) will catch this at DEV/REVIEW time regardless.

openQuestions.q: Does CHK-007's per-dispatch budget cap (LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS reused via shouldBlockDispatch) apply per-provider or globally across concurrently in-flight host runs, and is it a single-call ceiling or a rolling window?
openQuestions.evidence: checklist.json CHK-007 and plan.md describe reusing the existing shouldBlockDispatch/recordBudgetBlock guard without redefining its semantics; the plan does not state whether the cap is evaluated per-call (as today) or needs new cross-run aggregation now that host_run introduces a new call site alongside dispatch_run. Not a gap since the plan explicitly scopes this as reuse, not redefinition, but flagging since it is the first time this guard fires from a second call site.
